alt: Concrete elevated freeway structure in central Cape Town ending abruptly in mid-air, photographed looking east, with CBD buildings visible in the background — the famous 'bridge to nowhere' abandoned since 1977
story: Cape Town's Foreshore Freeway Bridge — a concrete elevated highway started in the early 1970s and abandoned unfinished in 1977 when the city ran out of money — has dangled over the CBD for nearly 50 years as a famous 'bridge to nowhere'; on October 2, 2026, Mayor Hill-Lewis unveiled the city's 'solution': build new alternative links over the next decade-plus, then demolish the old bridge.
why_funny: After half a century of a concrete highway hanging in mid-air, the official fix is a multi-decade plan to build a different structure nearby, then tear down the dangling original.
